title: Psalm 139 — YHWH has searched me and known me

verdicts.reasoning: lamnaṣṣēaḥ lĕdāwid mizmôr YHWH ḥăqartanî wattēdāʿ: superscription run into v 1 (MT = ASV numbering here), verified. Exact.
ʾattâ yādaʿtā šibtî wĕqûmî bantâ lĕrēʿî mērāḥôq: rēaʿ II 'thought' (Aramaizing). Exact.
ʾorḥî wĕribʿî zērîtā ... hiskantâ: zrh 'winnow' → 'search out' (ASV). Exact.

kî ʾên millâ bilšônî hēn YHWH yādaʿtā kullāh: ASV construction kept (no supplied 'before'); the temporal paraphrase of the canon's French is recorded, and the reception note does not move the line toward 'telepathy'. Exact.
ʾāḥôr wāqedem ṣartānî wattāšet ʿālay kappekâ: ṣwr 'hem in'. Exact.
Source checked: Ketiv פלאיה, Qere פְּלִיאָה (orthographic). Verbless clause rendered without the ASV's supplied 'Such'. Exact.
ʾānâ ʾēlēk mērûḥekā wĕʾānâ mippāneykā ʾebrāḥ: lower-case 'spirit' || 'presence' (NRSV, NJPS). Exact.
ʾim-ʾessaq šāmayim šām ʾāttâ wĕʾaṣṣîʿâ šĕʾôl hinnekkā: 'heavens' (cosmic height against She'ol, cf. Amos 9:2) under the founder's register ruling; 'She'ol' transliterated (central). Exact.
ʾeśśāʾ kanpê-šaḥar ʾeškĕnâ bĕʾaḥărît yām. 'dawn' as job-woh 38:12. Exact.
gam-šām yādĕkā tanḥēnî wĕtōʾḥăzēnî yĕmînekā. Exact.
wāʾōmar ʾak-ḥōšek yĕšûpēnî: MT šwp kept with ASV 'overwhelm', emendation yĕśukkēnî (NRSV 'cover') recorded. Correct MT-baseline application.
gam-ḥōšek lōʾ-yaḥšîk mimmekkā ... kaḥăšêkâ kāʾôrâ. Exact.

citations: HALOT s.v. skk II; s.v. qnh
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed: kî-ʾattâ qānîtā kilyōtāy tĕsukkēnî bĕbeṭen ʾimmî. qnh 'create' in a womb-formation context (NJPS 'created'; HALOT lists the create sense for this verse); tĕsukkēnî from skk II 'weave' with Job 10:11 (BDB, HALOT), NRSV 'knit me together'. The ASV 'covered' (skk I) is recorded. Both choices rest on the lexica; neither is lens.
ʾôdĕkā ʿal kî nôrāʾôt niplêtî ...: MT first person kept ('I am fearfully and wonderfully made', ASV), with the second-person reading of LXX/Syriac/Jerome (RSV) recorded; nepeš 'soul' as self. Exact.
lōʾ-nikḥad ʿoṣmî mimmekkā ... ruqqamtî bĕtaḥtiyyôt ʾāreṣ: rqm 'weave in colours'; 'the lowest parts of the earth'. Exact.

Source checked: Ketiv ולא, Qere וְלוֹ. Qere translated ('and for it there was one among them'); the ASV's Ketiv rendering is recorded. The literal Qere is obscure but honest, and the note flags the verse as one of the most uncertain in the Psalter.
wĕlî mah-yyāqĕrû rēʿeykā ʾēl: rēaʿ 'thought' (as v 2), ʾēl 'El' (extended shaddai-eloah). Exact.
ʾespĕrēm mēḥôl yirbbûn hĕqîṣōtî wĕʿôdî ʿimmāk: MT qyṣ 'I awake' kept, emendation recorded. Exact.
ʾim-tiqṭōl ʾĕlôah rāšāʿ: optative ʾim; 'Eloah' as Job. Exact.
ʾăšer yōʾmĕrukā limzimmâ nāśuʾ laššāwʾ ʿāreykā: ʿār 'enemy' (Aramaizing); object 'your name' supplied with the ASV and declared in commentary. Defensible.
hălôʾ-mĕśanʾeykā YHWH ʾeśnāʾ ûbitqômĕmeykā ʾetqôṭāṭ. Exact.
taklît śinʾâ śĕnēʾtîm lĕʾôyĕbîm hāyû lî. Exact.
ḥoqrēnî ʾēl wĕdaʿ lĕbābî bĕḥānēnî wĕdaʿ śarʿappāy: 'El', inclusio with v 1. Exact.
ûrĕʾēh ʾim-derek-ʿōṣeb bî ûnĕḥēnî bĕderek ʿôlām: ASV/NRSV 'wicked way' with the two ʿōṣeb senses and 'ancient way' recorded. Exact.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Philologically neutral and correctly direct: a typographic convention, with the Hebrew form standing in the source text and every name verified (David, Solomon, Jerusalem, Zion, Israel, Jacob, Job). Flagged only because it is founder point D (the corpus split with the Kings transliteration). Reviewer view: accept English forms for the Writings. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, which are not retro-edited, and the four books must agree with each other. Record the genre split (narrative transliterated, poetry English) as deliberate, or settle it corpus-wide in one later decision.

Every site verified: YHWH; 'Yah' (Ps 147:1, 20); the article follows the Hebrew (anarthrous Ps 8:6; Eccl 3:10, 13; articular Eccl 3:11, 14, 15, 17, 18); 'El', 'Eloah' and 'Shaddai' as in stable job-woh (38:41; 40:2, 9); 'our Lord' for ʾădōnênû. Direct is right: these are presentation rules over explicit Hebrew forms. Flagged only for founder point A (Ps 8:6 'Elohim' against the canon's 'the Elohim'). Reviewer view: keep the anarthrous form. The Hebrew has no article, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and the Kings clause 2, and departing from the canon's wording here is evidence that the line is not canon-driven.

Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974), ch. 2
glossaryReview.reasoning: The 'life' / 'soul' split was checked at all six sites. 'life' where a life is delivered from death or forfeited (Ps 33:19 || 'keep them alive'; Prov 8:36 in the life/death antithesis), as in the Kings and Ezekiel overlays. ASV 'soul' is kept for the self (Ps 19:8; 33:20; 139:14; Prov 10:3), with the appetite sense in commentary. Direct is defensible: BDB lists both senses.

Inferred is the honest class: the traditional English of Eccl 3:21 is 'spirit'. The lexical evidence is real. BDB and HALOT give rûaḥ 'breath (of life)'; NJPS has 'lifebreath' at Eccl 3:21; and vv 19-21 argue about the one rûaḥ that humans and beasts share (Gen 6:17; 7:15, 22). Lower-case 'spirit' at Ps 139:7 follows NRSV and NJPS. 'wind' (Job 37:21; Ps 147:18) and 'breath of his mouth' (Ps 33:6) are uncontroversial.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012)
glossaryReview.reasoning: All six pairs were verified in the Leningrad source (Job 37:12; Ps 139:6, 16; 147:19; Prov 8:17, 35), and all Qere are translated. The ASV-follows-Ketiv statements at Ps 139:16 and 147:19 are correct. No seventh pair exists: Prov 8:16 is a manuscript variant, as the editor says. Direct is correct.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.
The ASV terms are accurate, and the uncertainty is honestly stated: lamnaṣṣēaḥ (Piel ptc. nṣḥ), mizmôr, Gittith, and the ambiguity of lĕdāwid. Direct is appropriate.
BDB places Ps 139:13 under sākak II 'weave together' with Job 10:11, and HALOT likewise; NRSV 'knit me together'; v 15 ruqqamtî continues the weaving image. Direct is justified by lexical consensus.

The content is approved. The appended rationale treats Prov 8:22 honestly as the most contested site (ASV, Aquila/Symmachus/Theodotion, Vulgate and Vawter for 'acquire'; LXX, Targum, Peshitta, NRSV and NJPS for 'created') and says that the direct class rests on the Gen 14 epithet, not on Prov 8:22. Ps 139:13 'created' is supported by NJPS and HALOT. The diff appends text to the base unchanged (verified). One mechanical fix: the appended wohChoice is joined without punctuation ('creator of heaven and earth Verbal clause ...'). Apply it as 'creator of heaven and earth. Verbal clause (Writings wave W1): ...'.

Append-only (verified). It extends the stable job-woh practice for bare ʾēl ('El', 38:41; 40:9) to Job 37 and to Ps 19:2; 139:17, 23, and 'Eloah' to Ps 139:19, and it names the isaiah-woh 'God' exception explicitly. All appliesTo sites were checked against the Hebrew.
appliesTo +12 matches appliesToAdded exactly (verified against base); every site carries the ref and follows the register rule.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: All 24 lines checked. 139:4-6 keep the ASV construction (no temporal 'before'), and 'knowledge' renders daʿat; the 'telepathy' reading is in the note only. 139:13 'created' / 'knit me together' rest on HALOT/BDB/NJPS/NRSV. No flags.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 205 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 16 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, the Leningrad source files, the overlays, the diff, the 2.83.0 base and the canon-quotation file before wave-w1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's list of the three canon-coincident lines (section 1) confirmed the two commentary revisions: at Job 37:18 and Prov 8:30 the notes cite only the canon's French, whose wording matches the line, and omit the canon's English ('the sky'; 'as one brought up with him'), which does not. Prov 8:22 already shows the correct treatment. The report's six-pair Ketiv/Qere count was independently confirmed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-Ps-8:6-article-on-Elohim: Keep 'a little less than Elohim' without the article. The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-bene-(ha)adam: Accept 'the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human' for coherence with central ha-adam / ben-adam and GEN-WOH-11:5, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 ('the children of men') to it. The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. If the founder prefers idiom, revert every plural site together to 'the sons of men' (string swap; drop the plural refIds from the ha-adam and ben-adam ops). Do not mix the two.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-eretz-cosmic-earth: Agree. Promote the 'earth' scope clause (isaiah-woh + Writings) to central eretz in a dedicated later diff, after the parallel appliesTo merges have landed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-proper-names: Accept English forms in the four Writings books. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, and the four books must agree. Record the corpus practice as genre-split (narrative transliterated, poetry and prophets English) or settle it in one corpus-wide decision. Do not leave it implicit.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-chesed-kindness: Confirm 'kindness' for solitary ḥesed now, before the Psalter grows (about 120 occurrences). It is the central wohChoice, consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and lexically sound (Glueck; Sakenfeld). The loyalty sense stays in commentary, and the fixed pair ḥesed wĕʾĕmet stays under chesed-v-emet.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-Job-37:18-clouds: No decision needed: 'clouds' rests on BDB/HALOT, KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and 'strong' (not 'solid') keeps the line neutral. The reviewer asks for one transparency sentence (JOB-WOH-37:18 revise; shechaqim op revise): the canon's English edition reads 'the sky', so the canon is itself divided.

reviewerReport.summary: 24 verdicts: 24 approve, 0 revise, 0 flag-for-human. Glossary items relevant to this chapter: 14 (11 approve, 1 revise, 2 flag-for-human); not approved: proper-names-english-forms-convention-writings (flag-for-human); divine-names-convention-writings (flag-for-human); koneh-shamayim-va-aretz (revise). No lens leakage in any line. Flags are founder-confirmation points (A, B, D, E). Revisions are factual or mechanical. Status awaiting-human.

paragraphs.text: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ לְדָוִ֣ד מִזְמ֑וֹר יְהוָ֥ה חֲ֝קַרְתַּ֗נִי וַתֵּדָֽע׃

i18n.en: For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. YHWH, you have searched me and known me.

notes.official: Here the MT runs the superscription (*lamnaṣṣēaḥ lĕdāwid mizmôr* 'For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David') into v 1, so the MT and ASV verse numbers coincide. The heading is translated within v 1 (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`; `psalm-superscription-terms-psalms`). *ḥăqartanî wattēdāʿ* 'you have searched me and known me': *ḥqr* is to search out, explore. The closing prayer of v 23 (*ḥoqrēnî ... wĕdaʿ*) answers it.

paragraphs.text: אַתָּ֣ה יָ֭דַעְתָּ שִׁבְתִּ֣י וְקוּמִ֑י בַּ֥נְתָּה לְ֝רֵעִ֗י מֵרָחֽוֹק׃

i18n.en: You know my sitting down and my rising up; you understand my thought from afar.

notes.official: *rēʿî* 'my thought' is an Aramaizing noun (BDB *rēaʿ* II), the same word as *rēʿeykā* in v 17. *mērāḥôq* 'from afar'.

paragraphs.text: אָרְחִ֣י וְרִבְעִ֣י זֵרִ֑יתָ וְֽכָל־דְּרָכַ֥י הִסְכַּֽנְתָּה׃

i18n.en: My path and my lying down you search out, and you are acquainted with all my ways.

notes.official: *ʾorḥî wĕribʿî zērîtā* 'My path and my lying down you search out': *zrh* is literally 'winnow, sift' (ASV 'searchest out'). *hiskantâ* 'you are acquainted with'.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י אֵ֣ין מִ֭לָּה בִּלְשׁוֹנִ֑י הֵ֥ן יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָדַ֥עְתָּ כֻלָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: For there is not a word on my tongue, but behold, YHWH, you know it altogether.

notes.official:
*kî ʾên millâ bilšônî hēn YHWH yādaʿtā kullāh* 'For there is not a word on my tongue, but behold, YHWH, you know it altogether' (ASV construction). NRSV and NJPS take the clause temporally ('Before a word is on my tongue'), a fair paraphrase of the same Hebrew; the line keeps the ASV construction, which does not add 'before'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 4-6 in a French wording with the temporal sense ('la parole n'est pas encore sur ma langue, que déjà, Iahvé, tu la connais toute') and reads the passage as an allusion to telepathy, a knowledge unimaginable at that time ('Such knowledge is too wonderful for me'). The lines render the Hebrew: *millâ* is 'word', and v 6 names *daʿat* 'knowledge'.

paragraphs.text: אָח֣וֹר וָקֶ֣דֶם צַרְתָּ֑נִי וַתָּ֖שֶׁת עָלַ֣י כַּפֶּֽכָה׃

i18n.en: Behind and before you have hemmed me in, and laid your hand upon me.

notes.official: *ʾāḥôr wāqedem ṣartānî* 'Behind and before you have hemmed me in' (*ṣwr* 'besiege, enclose'; ASV 'beset'); *wattāšet ʿālay kappekâ* 'and laid your hand upon me' (*kap* 'palm'). See the reception note at v 4.

paragraphs.text: פלאיה [פְּלִ֣יאָֽה] דַ֣עַת מִמֶּ֑נִּי נִ֝שְׂגְּבָ֗ה לֹא־א֥וּכַֽל לָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Knowledge too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain to it.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *plʾyh* (a feminine adjective form) / Qere *pĕlîʾâ* 'wonderful'. The two do not differ in sense, and the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-writings`). *pĕlîʾâ daʿat mimmennî* is a verbless clause and is rendered without the ASV's supplied '[Such]': 'Knowledge too wonderful for me'. *niśgĕbâ* 'it is high', out of reach. See the reception note at v 4.

paragraphs.text: אָ֭נָ֥ה אֵלֵ֣ךְ מֵרוּחֶ֑ךָ וְ֝אָ֗נָה מִפָּנֶ֥יךָ אֶבְרָֽח׃

i18n.en: Where shall I go from your spirit, or where shall I flee from your presence?

notes.official: *mērûḥekā* 'from your spirit' || *mippāneykā* 'from your presence' (lit. 'face'). YHWH's *rûaḥ* is lower-case 'spirit', as in the isaiah-woh overlay. The ASV capital 'Spirit' reads a later doctrine into the Hebrew (`ruach-wind-breath-spirit-writings`).

paragraphs.text: אִם־אֶסַּ֣ק שָׁ֭מַיִם שָׁ֣ם אָ֑תָּה וְאַצִּ֖יעָה שְּׁא֣וֹל הִנֶּֽךָּ׃

i18n.en: If I go up to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in She'ol, behold, you are there.

notes.official: *ʾim-ʾessaq šāmayim ... wĕʾaṣṣîʿâ šĕʾôl* 'If I go up to the heavens ... if I make my bed in She'ol': the vertical extremes of the cosmos (cf. Amos 9:2). *šāmayim* as the height above all things is 'the heavens', as for Elijah's ascent at 2 Kgs 2:1, 11 (central `shamayim`; `shamayim-register-application-writings`). *šĕʾôl* is transliterated under the central `sheol-underworld-realm-of-the-dead` (ASV 'Sheol').

paragraphs.text: אֶשָּׂ֥א כַנְפֵי־שָׁ֑חַר אֶ֝שְׁכְּנָ֗ה בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית יָֽם׃

i18n.en: If I take the wings of the dawn, and dwell in the farthest part of the sea,

notes.official: *kanpê-šaḥar* 'the wings of the dawn' (job-woh 38:12 'dawn'; ASV 'morning'); *bĕʾaḥărît yām* 'in the farthest part of the sea', the far west. East and west complete the span of v 8.

paragraphs.text: גַּם־שָׁ֭ם יָדְךָ֣ תַנְחֵ֑נִי וְֽתֹאחֲזֵ֥נִי יְמִינֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me.

paragraphs.text: וָ֭אֹמַר אַךְ־חֹ֣שֶׁךְ יְשׁוּפֵ֑נִי וְ֝לַ֗יְלָה א֣וֹר בַּעֲדֵֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And if I say, "Surely the darkness will overwhelm me, and the light around me will be night,"

notes.official: *ʾak-ḥōšek yĕšûpēnî* 'Surely the darkness will overwhelm me' (ASV). The verb *šwp* elsewhere means 'bruise, crush' (Gen 3:15; Job 9:17), and the rationale of the central `shuf-rosh-aqev` cites this verse. Many emend to *yĕśukkēnî* 'will cover me' (NRSV). The line keeps the MT verb with the ASV's contextual rendering (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). *wāʾōmar* 'And if I say' (lit. 'and I said'); *wĕlaylâ ʾôr baʿădēnî* 'and the light around me will be night'.

paragraphs.text: גַּם־חֹשֶׁךְ֮ לֹֽא־יַחְשִׁ֪יךְ מִ֫מֶּ֥ךָ וְ֭לַיְלָה כַּיּ֣וֹם יָאִ֑יר כַּ֝חֲשֵׁיכָ֗ה כָּאוֹרָֽה׃

i18n.en: even the darkness is not dark to you, but the night shines like the day; darkness and light are alike.

notes.official: *kaḥăšêkâ kāʾôrâ* 'darkness and light are alike' (lit. 'as the darkness, so the light').

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־אַ֭תָּה קָנִ֣יתָ כִלְיֹתָ֑י תְּ֝סֻכֵּ֗נִי בְּבֶ֣טֶן אִמִּֽי׃

i18n.en: For you created my inward parts; you knit me together in my mother's womb.

notes.official:
*kî-ʾattâ qānîtā kilyōtāy* 'For you created my inward parts'. *qnh* has the sense 'create, produce' here, under the central `koneh-shamayim-va-aretz` entry, whose rationale cites this verse among the Hebrew attestations of that sense (ASV 'didst form'; NRSV 'formed'; NJPS 'created'). *kilyôt* 'kidneys' stand for the innermost self.

*tĕsukkēnî bĕbeṭen ʾimmî* 'you knit me together in my mother's womb'. The ASV 'thou didst cover me' derives the verb from *skk* I 'screen, cover'. BDB and HALOT list this verse with Job 10:11 ('with bones and sinews you knit me together', *tĕsōkĕkēnî*) under *skk* II 'weave', and NRSV ('knit me together') follows. The weaving image continues in v 15 (*ruqqamtî* 'intricately wrought'). The line follows the lexica (`sakhak-knit-together-psalm-139-13`).

paragraphs.text: אֽוֹדְךָ֗ עַ֤ל כִּ֥י נוֹרָא֗וֹת נִ֫פְלֵ֥יתִי נִפְלָאִ֥ים מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י יֹדַ֥עַת מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: I give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made; wonderful are your works, and my soul knows it very well.

notes.official: *ʾôdĕkā ʿal kî nôrāʾôt niplêtî* 'I give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made' (MT *niplêtî*, Niphal of *plh* / *plʾ* 'be set apart, be wonderful'). The LXX, the Syriac and Jerome read *niplêtā* 'you are fearfully wonderful'; the MT is translated (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`). *wĕnapšî yōdaʿat mĕʾōd* 'and my soul knows it very well': *nepeš* as the self (`nefesh-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: לֹא־נִכְחַ֥ד עָצְמִ֗י מִ֫מֶּ֥ךָּ אֲשֶׁר־עֻשֵּׂ֥יתִי בַסֵּ֑תֶר רֻ֝קַּ֗מְתִּי בְּֽתַחְתִּיּ֥וֹת אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: My frame was not hidden from you when I was made in secret, intricately wrought in the lowest parts of the earth.

notes.official: *lōʾ-nikḥad ʿoṣmî mimmekkā* 'My frame was not hidden from you': *ʿōṣem* 'bone(s), substance' (ASV 'frame'). *ruqqamtî* 'I was intricately wrought' (*rqm* 'weave in colors, embroider'; ASV 'curiously wrought'). *bĕtaḥtiyyôt ʾāreṣ* 'in the lowest parts of the earth' pictures the womb as the depths of the earth (cf. Job 1:21), so 'earth', not 'land' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: גָּלְמִ֤י ׀ רָ֘א֤וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל־סִפְרְךָ֮ כֻּלָּ֪ם יִכָּ֫תֵ֥בוּ יָמִ֥ים יֻצָּ֑רוּ ולא [וְל֖וֹ] אֶחָ֣ד בָּהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Your eyes saw my unformed substance, and in your book all of them were written — the days that were formed, and for it there was one among them.

notes.official: *gālmî* (hapax) 'my unformed substance' (ASV), the embryo; later Hebrew *gōlem* is an unshaped mass. Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *wlʾ* 'and not' / Qere *wĕlô* 'and to it'. The Qere is translated, 'and for it there was one among them', each day assigned (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-writings`). The ASV ('when as yet there was none of them') follows the Ketiv. *kullām* 'all of them' may point forward to *yāmîm* 'the days' or back to the members of the embryo. *yuṣṣārû* 'were formed' (ASV 'ordained'). The verse is among the most uncertain in the Psalter (Allen, WBC 21; Kraus, *Psalms 60-150*).

paragraphs.text: וְלִ֗י מַה־יָּקְר֣וּ רֵעֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑ל מֶ֥ה עָ֝צְמוּ רָאשֵׁיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And to me, how precious are your thoughts, El! How vast is the sum of them!

notes.official: *mah-yāqĕrû rēʿeykā ʾēl* 'how precious are your thoughts, El!': *rēaʿ* 'thought' as in v 2 (ASV). The common noun *rēaʿ* 'friend' would give 'your friends', but vv 17-18 count the *rēʿîm* like sand, which suits 'thoughts'. *ʾēl* is transliterated 'El' (central `shaddai-eloah`, extended in this wave; `divine-names-convention-writings`). *ʿāṣĕmû rāʾšêhem* 'how vast is the sum of them' (*rōʾš* 'sum').

paragraphs.text: אֶ֭סְפְּרֵם מֵח֣וֹל יִרְבּ֑וּן הֱ֝קִיצֹ֗תִי וְעוֹדִ֥י עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: If I count them, they are more than the sand. I awake, and I am still with you.

notes.official: *hĕqîṣōtî wĕʿôdî ʿimmāk* 'I awake, and I am still with you' (MT, from *qyṣ* 'awake'; ASV 'When I awake'). Many emend to *haqiṣṣōtî* 'I come to the end' (from *qṣṣ*; NRSV). The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`).

paragraphs.text: אִם־תִּקְטֹ֖ל אֱל֥וֹהַּ ׀ רָשָׁ֑ע וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י דָ֝מִ֗ים ס֣וּרוּ מֶֽנִּי׃

i18n.en: If only you would slay the wicked, Eloah! — and you men of blood, depart from me —

notes.official: *ʾim-tiqṭōl ʾĕlôah rāšāʿ* 'If only you would slay the wicked, Eloah!': *ʾim* introduces a wish. *ʾĕlôah* is transliterated 'Eloah', as in Job (central `shaddai-eloah`). *ʾanšê dāmîm* 'men of blood'.

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֹ֭אמְרֻךָ לִמְזִמָּ֑ה נָשֻׂ֖א לַשָּׁ֣וְא עָרֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: who speak of you with wicked intent; your enemies take your name in vain.

notes.official: *ʾăšer yōʾmĕrukā limzimmâ* 'who speak of you with wicked intent': *yōʾmĕrukā* is an irregular form of *ʾmr* with a suffix, and some read *yamrûkā* 'they rebel against you'. *nāśuʾ laššāwʾ ʿāreykā* 'your enemies take your name in vain': *ʿār* 'enemy' is Aramaizing (cf. 1 Sam 28:16; ASV 'thine enemies'), and *nśʾ laššāwʾ* is the idiom of Ex 20:7, where the object is 'the name of YHWH'. The object 'your name' is supplied, as in the ASV ('take [thy name] in vain'), because the English verb needs one (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`).

paragraphs.text: הֲלֽוֹא־מְשַׂנְאֶ֖יךָ יְהוָ֥ה ׀ אֶשְׂנָ֑א וּ֝בִתְקוֹמְמֶ֗יךָ אֶתְקוֹטָֽט׃

i18n.en: Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? And do I not loathe those who rise up against you?

paragraphs.text: תַּכְלִ֣ית שִׂנְאָ֣ה שְׂנֵאתִ֑ים לְ֝אוֹיְבִ֗ים הָ֣יוּ לִֽי׃

i18n.en: I hate them with complete hatred; they have become my enemies.

paragraphs.text: חָקְרֵ֣נִי אֵ֭ל וְדַ֣ע לְבָבִ֑י בְּ֝חָנֵ֗נִי וְדַ֣ע שַׂרְעַפָּֽי׃

i18n.en: Search me, El, and know my heart; test me, and know my anxious thoughts.

notes.official: *ḥoqrēnî ʾēl wĕdaʿ lĕbābî* 'Search me, El, and know my heart' returns to v 1 (`shaddai-eloah`). *śarʿappāy* 'my anxious thoughts' (cf. Ps 94:19).

paragraphs.text: וּרְאֵ֗ה אִם־דֶּֽרֶךְ־עֹ֥צֶב בִּ֑י וּ֝נְחֵ֗נִי בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ עוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: And see if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

notes.official: *derek-ʿōṣeb* 'any wicked way' (ASV, NRSV): *ʿōṣeb* is 'pain, hurt' (I) or 'idol' (II), and 'a hurtful way' or 'an idolatrous way' are possible. *bĕderek ʿôlām* 'in the way everlasting' (ASV), or 'the ancient way' (cf. Jer 6:16; 18:15).
